US financial-sector outperformance (HOOD, FUJI) is creating a sentiment halo for Indonesian brokers and payment processors, but local liquidity remains the binding constraint for sustained upside.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's downstreaming policy for solar glass and battery materials creates durable cost advantages for local players like TOBA and LAPD, insulating them from global price swings.
The shift of petrochemical majors like TPIA into green chemicals and carbon capture is a multi-year structural earnings driver, not a short-term trade.
US-listed climate-tech names (PLUG, ARKO) face persistent liquidity and execution risk; capital is better deployed in IDX-listed renewables with domestic demand tailwinds.
sectors.ai: Indonesia renewables remain a selective long: TOBA's +7.55% confirms downstream solar glass momentum, while TPIA's petchem-to-green pivot adds optionality. US names (PLUG, ARKO) are noise—ignore. Buy dips in TOBA and LAPD on any IDX weakness; avoid PKPK and MPOW until earnings confirm. Watch for policy catalysts from the new government's energy transition roadmap to re-rate the sector.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small-cap FMCG names are decoupling from large-cap indices, driven by domestic liquidity rotation into high-beta consumer stories with low institutional coverage.
US consumer strength (+1.00%) is a durable tailwind for Indonesian exporters of processed foods and personal care, as USD purchasing power boosts demand for premium local brands.
Structural shift toward food-away-from-home (NASI, CARS) and tech-enabled retail (NANO, BTEK) is accelerating, supported by rising urban middle-class spending and digital adoption.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG names showing volume-driven re-rating (AGAR, BTEK, NAYZ) while large caps lag; US strength (+1.00%) supports export-linked consumer plays. Rotate into food-service and specialty retail sub-sectors with earnings momentum, avoid broad index exposure. Target 3-6 week horizon, set tight stops at 5% below entry given normal signal volatility.

Prioritize large-cap US names (HCA, ZTS, BMY) over local healthcare, as US momentum and pipeline catalysts will outperform Indonesian regulatory overhangs in the next quarter.
